items_missed: 1_set_agenda: never asked 'how are you today?', skipped the agenda statement (what we'll cover + time estimate), and never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into questions.
2_probe: never asked about stairs/floors at either address, tight turns/narrow hallways, storage needs, additional stops, access/parking concerns, or moving stressors.
3_pricing: skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener, never mentioned Meet Your Mover, and never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee.
4_clock: never did an explicit sense-check ('does that make sense?') after explaining how the clock works.

5_estimate: covered typical time range and mover/truck count but never walked through specialty-item, walk-distance, or traffic variables, and didn't use a relatable equivalent like the school-bus reference.
6_save_your_ass: no prep speech at all — no mention that prep shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip.
7_quote_booking: never made a direct ask to lock in the date today (left it as 'reply or call me back'), and never explicitly asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' before the call ended.
9_bonus: no rapport-building humor or laugh moment, and skipped the 60-cents-per-pound baseline valuation piece of the insurance explanation.
top_strength: Alex was fully transparent about the day-of-week rate difference, running the numbers for both Sunday and Friday so Sarah could see exactly what the schedule flexibility would cost her, and he got ahead of the hidden-fees question before she asked: "you don't have to worry about sales tax, any credit card processing fees... we don't charge anything outside of what we quote on the call."
coaching_note: Alex, your pricing walkthrough is solid and transparent — the Friday-vs-Sunday comparison was genuinely useful for her decision. But you skipped the two pieces that build trust and protect the final bill: there's no agenda statement up front, so Sarah has no idea how long the call will take or what's coming, and there's zero Save Your Ass prep speech. That's the section most tied to move efficiency — a two-sentence add (prep ahead, consolidate loose items, take a carload yourself) protects both her wallet and your actual time on the job. Add it before you move into pricing next time.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative throughout, but the call is mostly one-way info delivery — affirmations like "good deal" and "sweet" repeat often without much genuine back-and-forth, though Sarah stayed warm and thankful by the end.
audio_review_reason: ASR garbles the actual dollar figures in the pricing section (e.g. "$38,444 man team") and there's a name mix-up mid-call — worth a listen to confirm the numbers quoted and rule out an audio issue.
